cases.name: parent-on-a-gen-instead-of-its-sequence
cases.description: parent= is read on <sequence> and <mix> and nowhere else. Accepting it on a <gen> made a config that plainly says "only build this where a == A" produce the value on every row, with nothing said. Refused, so the reader is pointed at the tag that reads it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="A,B"/></sequence><sequence name="b"><gen type="text" value="x" parent="a.A"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{a}}${{b}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: percent-on-a-switch-instead-of-a-mix
cases.description: A <switch> chooses its case from the value of on=, and <case> requires is= (TDC137), so there is no split for percent= to describe. It belongs to <mix>. It was on the accepted list and read by nobody.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="g"><gen type="text" value="M,F"/></sequence><switch name="s" on="g" percent="80"><case is="M"><data>m</data></case><case is="F"><data>f</data></case></switch></env><block><line><data>${{s}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: env-and-tdc-attributes-written-on-a-gen
cases.description: seed, engine, version and inject belong to <env> or <tdc>. The four ports kept ONE flat union of every attribute name in the language and used it to judge a <gen>, so all four passed this config while the reference refused it — the same input, a different answer, depending on which implementation you happened to run.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="A,B" seed="nope" engine="2"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{a}}</data></line></block></tdc>
